# phase-065 — Let users extend the REPL: `.alias` and `.macro`

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
`alias` and `macro` are both absent from src/repl/commands.rs (verified), so every repeated workflow is retyped in full: there is no short name for a long command and no way to record a sequence once and replay it. Ipp ships both (`.alias n cmd`, `.macro` define/list) for exactly this reason. The machinery is small — the command table already parses aliases (`:hist`, `:v`, `:f` work today), so user aliases are the same table with user rows — but the absence forces repetition onto every session.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Add `.alias <name> <command>` (user-named command shortcuts, listed in `:help`, shadowing nothing built in) and `.macro` (record the session's lines between start/stop, replay them by name, list them). Aliases and macros live in the session and die with it unless `:save`d; a name colliding with a builtin is refused.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-065
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `.alias ll :vars` makes `ll` behave exactly as `:vars` (outputs diffed, not eyeballed); `.alias :vars :help` is refused naming the collision with a builtin
- [ ] a recorded macro of three lines replays all three in order with identical outputs (asserted by diffing two transcripts); `.macro` with no recording in progress is a clean usage error
- [ ] aliases and macros appear in `:help` output under their own section (help-completeness pattern), and TAB completes user macro names as well as builtins
- [ ] `:save` persists aliases and macros and `:restore` brings them back (round-trip asserted on a session carrying one of each)
- [ ] edge_* tests cover an alias whose value is another alias (resolves, exactly one level, no infinite loop on `.alias a b` + `.alias b a` — refused as a cycle), a macro recording across `:reset` (recording survives, bindings do not), and `.alias` with no arguments (lists current aliases, empty list named as such)
